name: Daylio
one_liner: Daylio is a mood tracking journal app that uses icons instead of writing, making it easy to track emotions, activities, and mental health patterns.
best_for: People who want to track moods without writing
Those curious about patterns in their mental health
People working with therapists who want data to share
Anyone building mental health awareness habits
not_for: Those in crisis needing immediate care (call 988)
short_description: Daylio is a mood tracking journal app that uses icons instead of writing, making it easy to track emotions, activities, and mental health patterns.
long_description: Daylio is a popular mood tracking app designed for people who don't like writing. Instead of journaling, you select mood levels and activities using icons. The app shows patterns over time—which activities correlate with better moods, how you feel on different days, and long-term trends. Daily reminders help build tracking habits. Data can be exported and shared with therapists. The free version provides core tracking; premium ($2.99/mo) adds advanced statistics and unlimited entries. Daylio has been downloaded millions of times and is particularly popular with people who find traditional journaling burdensome.
patient_summary: Daylio makes mood tracking as easy as tapping a few icons. See which activities make you feel better or worse, track your moods over time, and spot patterns you might not notice otherwise.

pricing.notes: Basic tracking free. Premium for advanced features.

privacy.notes: Consumer app, not healthcare. Data stored on device and optional cloud backup.

faqs.q: How does Daylio mood tracking work?
faqs.a: Each day, select your mood level (great to awful) and tag activities you did. Daylio requires no writing—just tapping icons. Over time, the app shows patterns and correlations between activities and moods.
Basic mood tracking is free. Premium ($2.99/month or $35.99/year) adds unlimited entries per day, advanced statistics, automatic backups, and no ads. The free version works well for basic tracking.

faqs.q: Can I share Daylio data with my therapist?
faqs.a: Yes, Daylio allows exporting data as PDF or CSV files. Many people share mood reports with therapists to identify patterns and track progress between sessions.

Daylio shows which activities correlate with better or worse moods, mood trends over weeks/months, day-of-week patterns, and how consistent your mood tracking is. These insights help identify what supports your mental health.

how_clinicians_use_it: Assign as homework for patients to track mood between sessions
Have patients export reports to review together in session
Help patients identify activity-mood patterns to target in treatment
Monitor treatment progress through mood trends over time
clinician.implementation_notes: No clinician dashboard - patient shares exports manually. PDF and CSV export available. Consider for patients who find journaling overwhelming.
